ca_labyrinth_main.blurb: The main section of the Labyrinth, a maze of limestone boulders in the foothills near Columbia and Sonora. Twenty problems cover nearly every style: slab, stemming and steep, juggy hauls. Most are easy to moderate, roughly VB to V2, with a few in the V3 to V5 range and a couple of hard test pieces up to V8. This part of the maze has thinner tree cover than neighboring zones, so it dries quickly after rain but can feel warm on sunny days. Expect a tangled, hard-to-navigate layout, so bring a map and a spotter, and watch for poison oak.

ca_90_foot_wall.blurb: A tall, well-featured granite cliff in Eagle Creek Canyon on the west shore of Lake Tahoe, above Emerald Bay. About twenty one-pitch routes, mostly trad cracks and faces plus several top-rope lines, run from easy fifth class through the 5.8 to 5.9 range, with a solid block of 5.10 and 5.11. That mix makes it a favorite for learning crack climbing and for guides and groups. The wall catches sun through the middle of the day, so start early when it is cold and later when it is warm. It is very popular and often crowded, with big views of the bay from the top.
ca_90_foot_wall.parking_note: Leave the car in the Eagle Creek Canyon lot near Emerald Bay. It fills quickly, so arrive early on weekends and in summer.
ca_90_foot_wall.approach: Take the waterfall trail uphill from the lot, heading away from the bay, and keep right at the fork. Rather than following the trail's sharp turn, step onto the broad granite slab and continue straight. The cliff appears on your right after a short stretch.

ca_dog_dish_boulders.blurb: A cluster of sandstone boulders within the Magoos zone at Castle Rock State Park in the Santa Cruz Mountains. Twenty problems here include a tall V0 highball and a long traverse that follows the scooped pockets the boulder is named for. The spread is wide: plenty of easy problems around V0 to V2, a handful of moderates, and a run of hard lines from V6 up to V10. The Magoos area is mostly shaded and busy on weekends, with a short walk from the main lot. The sandstone is soft and easily damaged when damp, so skip it after rain.

ca_hill_top_area.blurb: The largest group of boulders on the rise above the entry road, part of the Melrose Boulders zone in north San Diego County. It holds twenty problems, nearly all of them friendly: most fall between VB and V2, with a few moderate lines around V3 and V4, and a short list of hard problems up to V8. Several boulders along the short walk-up carry graffiti and paint, which is part of the local character. Popular lines include Turf Wars, The Beehive and Shoot to Kill. It suits a quick session with a pad or two, and a good place to warm up before heading elsewhere in the zone.

ca_gorgeous_towers.blurb: A tall, shady cliff in the Upper Gorge of the Owens River Gorge near Bishop, in the Eastern Sierra. The climbing is almost all bolted sport, with two trad lines, and the rock quality is high. Grades run from 5.9 through 5.12, with the bulk of routes in the 5.11 range, so it suits solid intermediate and stronger climbers. Because the towers stay in shade for most of the day, they are a cool choice when the weather turns hot, and the namesake route, Gorgeous, is a local favorite. Parking is at the edge of the lot with the cliff in view from the car.

ca_lower_ridge.blurb: A bouldering zone on the lower side of Pine Mountain, in the Ojai and Highway 33 area of the Los Padres backcountry. The mountain is a sandstone boulder field strung along a ridge for several miles, and this lower section lies below the Happy Hunting Grounds, lower on the slope. About twenty problems here are mostly short and easygoing, with most between VB and V4, then a few harder lines reaching V8. Sock Hop is a known problem in this part of the ridge. It is a quiet area for climbers who like to wander between boulders, and it pairs well with a camping trip on top.

ca_mountain_view_wall_south.blurb: The southern half of Mountain View Wall, a steep granite crag above Mammoth Lakes with views toward the Minarets. About twenty routes mix sport and trad, running from 5.10 up to a single 5.13, with most between 5.11 and 5.12, so it is mainly for experienced climbers. The face looks west, and tall conifers at its base keep it shaded longer in the morning than the north wall, though a few lines get shade again later in the afternoon. The climbing is often steep and physical, and the bolted lines use stainless hardware.
ca_mountain_view_wall_south.approach: Walk the Starkweather Trail from near Minaret Vista and drop into the gully of sand between the two walls. The south wall is a couple of minutes further, bearing left.
